diagnostics.message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
kubernetes_service_account_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup is created in namespace var.controller_config.namespace, but that namespace is only created by the scale_set_controller module (resource.kubernetes_namespace.controller_namespace, under the same migrate_arc_cluster == false condition). On a fresh apply the ServiceAccount can be applied before the namespace exists, failing the apply with a 404. It should depend on the namespace resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
The zombie-runner-cleanup service account (and the Role/RoleBinding/CronJob that reference it) is created in var.controller_config.namespace, but nothing orders it after that namespace is actually created. In module.controller the namespace is provisioned by kubernetes_namespace.controller_namespace (and, for the controller chart, via create_namespace = true on the helm release). The zombie-runner-cleanup resources have no attribute reference to any of these, so on a fresh apply the service account can race the namespace creation and fail with a "namespace not found" API error. An explicit depends_on on the controller's namespace resource closes this gap; the Role, RoleBinding, and CronJob are transitively ordered behind the service account, so the dependency only needs to be added once.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
kubernetes_service_account_v1.zombie_runner_cleanup (and the role/role-binding/cron-job that reference it) are created in namespace var.controller_config.namespace, which is provisioned by module.controller's kubernetes_namespace.controller_namespace (and otherwise only by the controller helm_release's create_namespace=true). Nothing ties the root-module zombie resources to that namespace resource, so on a fresh apply Terraform may attempt to create the service account before the namespace exists and fail with "namespaces \"arc\" not found". An ordering dependency on the controller namespace is missing.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set deploys the runner scale set whose listener consumes the hook-extension ConfigMap (hook-extension-<scale_set_name>, provided by the chart's listener hook mechanism by naming convention). If the release is installed before kubernetes_config_map.hook_extension exists, the listener starts without the hook extension and the container-podspec overrides are silently not applied until a later listener restart. The release should depend on the ConfigMap.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The runner scale set Helm chart consumes the hook ConfigMaps ("hook-extension-<scale_set_name>" and "hook-pre-post-job-<scale_set_name>") created by kubernetes_config_map.hook_extension and kubernetes_config_map.hook_pre_post_job. The helm_release only references var.scale_set_name/var.service_account strings in its values template, so Terraform may install the release before these ConfigMaps exist, leaving the runners without their hook configuration. An ordering dependency on both ConfigMaps is missing.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set deploys the runner scale set whose listener consumes the pre/post-job hook scripts from the ConfigMap named hook-pre-post-job-<scale_set_name> by convention. If the release is installed before kubernetes_config_map.hook_pre_post_job exists, the job-started/job-completed hooks are not picked up when the listener is created. The release should depend on the ConfigMap.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
Same as hook_extension: the "job_started.sh"/"job_completed.sh" hook scripts in kubernetes_config_map.hook_pre_post_job must exist before the gha_runner_scale_set Helm release is installed, otherwise the runner pods reference hook ConfigMaps that don't exist yet. No attribute reference or depends_on establishes this ordering.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set creates runner pods that run under the service account pre-created by kubernetes_service_account_v1.runner_sa (referenced only by name via the service_account variable in the chart values, so Terraform cannot infer ordering). On a fresh apply the scale set could be installed before the ServiceAccount exists, causing the runner/listener pods to fail to schedule. The release should depend on the ServiceAccount.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set installs the runner scale set whose pods run as the service account "runner_sa" (referenced by name via var.service_account in the chart values). If the release is applied before the Kubernetes service account exists, the listener deployment/runner pods will fail to schedule with a "serviceaccount not found" error, even though the Helm release itself reports success. The release must be ordered after the service account, but no attribute reference or depends_on expresses this.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set creates runner pods that assume the runner IAM role via EKS Pod Identity. aws_eks_pod_identity_association.eks_pod_identity must exist before the scale set's pods start, otherwise runners launch without IAM credentials and fail AWS API calls (e.g. pulling from ECR). There is no attribute reference between the release and the association (the values only reference the role ARN), so the release should depend on the association.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
The runner scale set helm_release only references aws_iam_role.runner_role.arn (through its values), but the runner pods it deploys rely on aws_eks_pod_identity_association.eks_pod_identity for their AWS credentials: per the AWS docs, pods using the associated service account get Pod Identity credentials injected, which the runners need for AWS API access (e.g. ECR pulls). The helm release has no dependency on the association, so the runners can be installed before the association exists and come up without IAM credentials. The chart's async install means there is no attribute reference that would order this naturally, so an explicit depends_on is the appropriate fix.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_eks_pod_identity_association.eks_pod_identity injects IAM credentials into pods using service account var.service_account in namespace var.namespace — the exact pods created by the gha_runner_scale_set Helm release. Per the AWS documentation, pods only receive credentials if the association exists. The helm_release references the IAM role ARN but not the association, so on a fresh apply the runner/listener pods can start before credentials are available and never pick them up until restarted. The release must depend on the association.
